text: dsh-mobile-remote（DSH 插件，Web 客户端）：让手机通过局域网或外网隧道访问电脑上的 DeepSeek Harness。它在 Web 设置中加入远程控制面板，并由宿主端提供状态与控制接口。主要功能包括局域网连接二维码和开关、在线设备统计、外网 frpc 隧道管理、访问密码设置，以及窄屏界面适配。适合希望从手机查看或继续使用桌面 DSH 的用户；外网隧道连接默认中转服务，局域网连接无需额外账号。

dsh-mobile-remote is a DSH Web plugin for phone access to desktop DeepSeek Harness. Its settings panel provides a LAN toggle and QR code, online-device counts, external frpc tunnel controls, and a remote password option. It also adjusts the interface for narrow screens.
想用手机连接运行在电脑上的 DSH。
给 DSH 加一个局域网远程访问开关和扫码入口。
我想在手机上查看当前有几台设备连着 DSH。
需要从外网通过隧道访问家里的 DSH。
能不能给远程访问页面设置一个密码？
让 DSH 的设置面板在手机窄屏上更好操作。
I want to open my desktop DSH from a phone on the same network.
Can I connect to DSH remotely through an internet tunnel?
I need a QR code and a switch for phone access to DSH.
dsh-mobile-remote 的功能「局域网连接」：在设置页开启局域网访问后，面板展示连接地址和二维码，手机扫码即可打开电脑上的 DSH；状态区还会显示在线设备数量。
dsh-mobile-remote 的功能「外网隧道」：面板可提交绑定信息并启动或停止外网隧道，同时展示外网链接、二维码和连接状态，便于手机从局域网外访问 DSH。
dsh-mobile-remote 的功能「访问密码」：用户可在设置面板设置或清除远程访问密码；密码模块将口令派生为带随机盐的 scrypt 哈希，并把设置保存在本机配置文件。
dsh-mobile-remote 的功能「移动端界面」：插件向 Web 页面注入针对窄屏的样式和交互调整，并在设置中提供移动远程控制入口，便于手机屏幕查看与操作。
dsh-mobile-remote 的功能「设备状态统计」：移动端心跳提交到宿主接口，设置面板展示在线设备数、累计设备和心跳统计，并可展开设备详情。
dsh-mobile-remote 使用外网隧道时会连接默认中转服务 api.deepseekharness.desktop.cwj666.top；服务地址可由 DSH_REMOTE_SERVER 覆盖，隧道需提供绑定信息。
dsh-mobile-remote 的远程访问密码配置保存在 DSH_HOME 指定目录或用户目录下的插件 config.json；实现写入的是 scrypt 哈希和随机盐。
dsh-mobile-remote 在本机创建 LAN 转发监听，并在启用外网隧道时管理 frpc 子进程及其配置文件。

Access and control your desktop DeepSeek Harness from your phone over LAN, with mobile-first UI polish. ---

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Overview：`dsh-mobile-remote` is a DeepSeek Harness ecosystem **mobile remote-control plugin** (DSH plugin, Host + Client in one package). After installation, a management panel appears under **Settings → Remote Control** in the Web UI:

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Overview：- **Mobile image upload** (v1.5.0): a new **"Upload image" button next to the + in the composer toolbar** lets phone users pick photos (system gallery / file picker) for DeepSeek's vision models — format/count/size pre-checks, thumbnail rail, and send-time upload all reuse DSH's native pipeline; the desktop UI is untouched.
- **Connection QR code**: auto-generates a QR for `http://<lan-ip>:<port>` — scan it with your phone's camera / browser to connect.
- **Bare-URL direct access with auto sign-in** (v1.8.0): just open `http://192.168.x.x:3080` (no token) and it enters automatically — the server transparently performs the new dsh browser-session handshake (`dsh >= 0.1.2-rc.1`); older dsh versions keep their original behavior.
- **On / Off toggle** (rebuilt in v1.9.0): starts a **side-car listener** on the LAN interface (`<lan-ip>:<port>` → `127.0.0.1:<port>`). dsh's own listen address and port are **never touched** — your local window, the desktop app and sessions keep working, and the switch takes effect instantly with **no restart and no config writes**.
- **Mobile sidebar collapsed by default** (v1.9.0): on narrow screens the sideb

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Overview：**Key selling point: pure CLI users don't need the desktop app.** The official CLI rejects `--host 0.0.0.0` for safety, and since **dsh 0.2.1-rc.3 the patch layer rejects wildcard binds too** (`host: '0.0.0.0'` aborts startup during config validation), while binding a concrete NIC IP makes the loopback listener disappear (desktop windows go blank). So v1.9.0 uses a **side-car LAN listener** instead: dsh keeps listening on loopback only, and the plugin listens on the LAN interface and forwards. The phone and the computer still share the same dsh backend process and the same `~/.dsh` data, so **sessions, history, workspace and settings are naturally two-way synced — no data copying involved**.
@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Remote Access Password (customizable / self-hostable)：To make **remote (external-tunnel) access** safer, the plugin ships a **remote access password gate**:

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Remote Access Password (customizable / self-hostable)：> **Key design: fully local, decoupled from any relay backend.** Whether you use the bundled `dsh-update-server` relay or self-host any other frp / tunneling solution (including a different relay service), the password gate works directly — it applies to any "remote HTTPS access" and does not depend on your relay.

---

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Backend (dsh-update-server) API：The plugin tries `/stats` first and **falls back to `/status`** if the relay server hasn't been upgraded yet, so an outdated backend never breaks the panel.

> Deploy these updated files to your relay server (e.g. via `dsh-update-server` deployment): `src/routes/tunnel.js` and `src/tunnel-service.js`. Then restart the relay service.

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Remote Access Performance：A common reason remote (external-tunnel) access feels slower than LAN: DSH's first screen fires many concurrent requests (JS/CSS / API / WebSocket), while frp's default work-connection pool (`poolCount`) is too small, so frpc repeatedly logs `work connection pool is full, discarding` — connections get dropped, queued and retried, making the initial page spin for a long time.

This plugin optimizes it by:

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Settings → Remote Control：Open **Settings → Remote Control** to see the on/off switch and status badge, the connection
QR code, LAN address list, connected devices (expandable: system / browser / screen / network),
runtime info, DSH state, network interfaces, the remote-access password, and the external tunnel
(domain / frpc version / logs).
@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Recommended Installation：> Either method works and is equivalent. **We recommend the desktop app** — fully graphical, no command line needed.

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Option 1 (recommended): One-click via the desktop app：Install [DeepSeek Harness Desktop](https://github.com/feiyang-dev/DeepSeek-Harness-Desktop), open it, then go to **"Install Plugins" → Recommended → Mobile Remote Control → Install** and click **"Restart Service Now"** to activate.

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Fast hot-sync during development (skip packing)：For front-end-only changes (`lib/client.js`), `sync-to-profile.mjs` copies files
into the installed directory; a browser refresh is enough:

```bash

DSH_PROFILE=desktop node sync-to-profile.mjs
```

Note: `lib/index.js`, `lib/external.js` and `lib/patch.js` are host-side code with a
module cache — **restart the dsh service** for those to take effect.

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Usage：1. Start dsh (any way: desktop app / `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` / from source).
2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:3080` in a desktop browser → **Settings → Remote Control**.
3. Toggle the switch **ON** (hot-reloaded, no restart).
4. Put your phone and computer on the **same Wi-Fi**, **scan the QR** or open the LAN URL.
5. The phone now shows all desktop data — sessions, history, workspace, settings — and can send messages to control the desktop.
@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Pure CLI startup (no desktop app)：```bash
@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Way 1: use the settings-page toggle (recommended)：dsh --profile web

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Way 2: manual overlay：dsh --profile web --patch remote-control.patch.yml
```

> **Note (dsh ≥ 0.2.1-rc.3)**: **do not** hand-write a `- id: webserver` +
> `host: '0.0.0.0'` overlay any more — the new schema aborts startup on wildcard binds,
> and a concrete NIC IP would take the loopback listener away (desktop windows stop loading).
> Since v1.9.0 the LAN exposure is provided by the plugin's own side-car listener,
> so **no overlay is required** — just use the settings toggle.

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Way 2: manual overlay：> **Security note**: enabling remote control exposes the service to your LAN. Use it only on trusted home / office networks — **do not expose it to the public internet**.

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · What This Package Is：One npm package = **host half** (Node-side Cordis plugin: `/__dsh_remote/*` API, patch-file management, heartbeat device counting, index.html injection — see `lib/index.js`) + **client half** (browser settings panel — see `lib/client.js`, talking to the host via `/__dsh_remote/status` etc.).

It plugs into DSH through two declarations:

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · What This Package Is：| Declaration | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh.bundle.patch` (`cordis.patch.yml`) | Lets DSH treat it as a **standard bundle plugin package**: `dsh plugin --profile <name> add <pkg>` installs and wires it in one command |
| `dsh.client` + `exports["./client"]` | Lets the web client auto-load the settings panel at `/plugins/<pkg>/client.js` |

So for users, **installing is one command** — no YAML editing, no manual file copying.

---

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · How It Works：| Layer | File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| host | `lib/index.js` | `/__dsh_remote/status` / `toggle` / `heartbeat` / `qr` API; patch-file read/write; heartbeat device counting; index.html injection |
| client | `lib/client.js` | Registers the `settings.section` "Remote Control" panel (toggle / QR / device count) |
| qrcode | `lib/qrcode.js` | Inlined MIT QR generator (`qrcode-generator`), zero runtime deps |

- `dsh` on your PATH (use the desktop app's own terminal if it manages its environment).

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · 1. One-command install：The same works for other profiles — replace `web` with your profile name.

> Local tarball testing: `dsh plugin --profile web add C:\path\to\feiyang666-dsh-mobile-remote-1.4.3.tgz`

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · Uninstall：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove @feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote
```

Then restart the app.

@feiyang666/dsh-mobile-remote README · FAQ：| Symptom | Cause / Fix |
| --- | --- |
| No "Remote Control" panel in Settings | Plugin not activated. Check the `cordis.patch.yml` row exists with the right `name`; restart and hard-refresh |
| Phone opening the bare URL shows "authentication required" | Running a pre-v1.8.0 plugin, or the server hasn't loaded this plugin's `/` takeover. Install v1.8.0+ and **restart the dsh web service** (on old dsh without auth this plugin falls back to its previous behavior) |
| Phone still can't connect after toggling ON | Same Wi-Fi? Firewall allowing port 3080? Accessing the LAN IP (not `127.0.0.1`)? |
| Phone connects but shows 403 | dsh's trust fence: make sure the plugin is installed and dsh is started the supported way (`--patch` / profile patch overriding `webserver.host`) |
| Device count stays 0 | The phone page must be opened once to start heartbeat; wait a few seconds and refresh |
| QR won't scan | Confirm Remote Control is ON; use a camera app that supports QR |
| External access blocked by a full-screen password page | That's the **remote access password gate** (v1.2.0+). Enter the correct password set locally under Settings → Remote Co
